title: Notifications and messages
subtitle: Reminders about important things, a daily summary and your details for e-mails. All free – no Przystań server.
enabledText: Off by default. When on, the app plans reminders from your data – on this device.
systemAndroid: The Android app schedules them in the system – they appear even when Przystań is closed.
systemWeb: In the browser and on the iPhone (PWA) a notification appears only when the app is opened – Apple does not let web apps schedule them without a server. For reminders while the app is closed use the calendar export below.

permission.denied: Notification permission: denied – change it in the phone / browser settings.
permission.unsupported: This browser does not support notifications.

exactText: Without this permission Android may deliver a reminder a few minutes late.
emailText: Sent through your own free EmailJS account (200 e-mails a month) when you open the app after the chosen time.
emailNeedsSetup: First fill in your e-mail address and the EmailJS details below.

rules.tasks: Tasks with a due date (also from supervision)
rules.ipr: IPR review (7 days before and when overdue)
rules.keyDates: Key dates of service users (14 days before)

privacy: What notifications and e-mails to yourself show
privacyHiddenText: Only counts and times – nothing anyone sees on the lock screen or at the mail provider points to a person.
privacyCodesText: Codes (e.g. KW-16) and meeting titles – never names.
meText: Encrypted together with your data, not included in backups.
myContact: Contact line in the signature (work phone / e-mail)
emailjsLead: EmailJS sends e-mails directly from the app through your mailbox (e.g. Gmail) – without a Przystań server. Free plan: 200 e-mails a month. Without EmailJS you can always send a message with your mail app.
emailjsHow: How to set up EmailJS (4 steps, about 5 minutes)
emailjsSteps: Create a free account at emailjs.com and add an e-mail service (e.g. Gmail) – that is the “Service ID”.
Create a template: “To Email” {{to_email}}, “Subject” {{subject}}, content {{message}}, “From Name” {{from_name}}, “Reply To” {{reply_to}}. Save – that is the “Template ID”.
Account → General: copy the “Public Key”. Enter the “Private Key” only if you turn on strict mode in EmailJS.
Paste the details below and send a test e-mail.
testEmail: Send a test e-mail to myself
testEmailBody: This is a test e-mail from Przystań. If you can see it, automatic e-mails work.
testEmailFail: Could not send (EmailJS: {{msg}}). Check the details and the template.
calendarText: Export planned meetings, IPR reviews and key dates to the phone's calendar (.ics file with alarms). On the iPhone this is the best way to get reminders while the app is closed. Export again after changes – the entries are updated.
testFailed: The notification could not be shown – allow notifications above.
previewSend: Send it to myself with the mail app
info: There is no automatic server SMS – paid gateways were ruled out. Free: SMS directly from this phone (Android app), through the free SMS Gateway for Android, or manually with the Messages app.

attention.noContact: No contact for a long time

digest.subject: Przystań – {{day}}
digest.hiddenNote: You will see the details in the app (this e-mail deliberately does not contain them).
digest.codesNote: This message contains only codes, no names.

gmail.title: E-mails from my Gmail (Google sign-in)
gmail.lead: Messages go out directly from your Gmail mailbox – no mail app and no intermediary. Przystań receives from Google only the permission “send on your behalf” (it cannot read your mail) for one hour.
gmail.clientIdHint: One-time setup – instructions below. The ID is not secret.
gmail.test: Send a test e-mail to myself
gmail.testBody: This is a test e-mail sent from Przystań directly from your Gmail. If you can see it, sending works.
gmail.howTo: How to set it up (once, about 10 minutes)
steps: Open console.cloud.google.com with the same Google account (you can use the project of your Gemini key).
“Google Auth Platform” → “Branding”: name “Przystań” and your e-mail; “Audience”: type “External”, status “Testing” → add the Gmail addresses you want to send from under “Test users”.
“Clients” → “Create client” → “Web application” → “Authorized JavaScript origins”: {{origin}} → copy the client ID and paste it above (PWA, browser).
For the Android app: “Create client” → “Android” → package name {{pkg}}, SHA-1 fingerprint: {{sha1}}.
On the first connection Google shows “unverified app” – it is your own setup: “Continue”. In testing mode Google may ask for consent again every 7 days.
gmail.privacy: The access token is kept in memory only (about 1 h) and never stored. Google sends the message from your account – you will find it under “Sent” in Gmail.

error.noClientId: First enter the OAuth client ID.
error.popup: The browser blocked the Google sign-in window – allow pop-ups.
error.denied: Google sign-in was cancelled or the permission was refused.
error.auth: Google did not grant the permission ({{msg}}). Check the Google Cloud setup.
error.unavailable: Google sign-in is not available right now.

sms.title: SMS directly from the app
sms.phoneOn: This phone can send SMS directly from Przystań – from your SIM card, within your plan. Android asks for permission with the first SMS.
sms.phoneWeb: Direct sending from the SIM works in the Android app (APK). On the iPhone and in the browser the SMS opens in the Messages app with the text ready.
sms.testPhone: Send a test SMS from this phone

error.DENIED: No permission to send SMS – allow it in phone Settings → Apps → Przystań → Permissions.
error.INVALID: Check the number and the text.
error.FAILED: The SMS could not be sent: {{msg}}

sms.gateTitle: Free SMS gateway (SMS Gateway for Android)
sms.gateLead: A free open-source app turns any Android phone into an SMS gateway – Przystań sends SMS through it from that phone’s SIM. The text passes through the sms-gate.app server – do not send sensitive data this way.
sms.gateWeb: The gateway works only from the Przystań Android app (its server does not allow calls from a browser).
sms.testGate: Send a test SMS through the gateway
sms.gateFail: The gateway did not send the SMS: {{msg}}
sms.gateHowTo: How to set up the gateway
gateSteps: On an Android phone install “SMS Gateway for Android” (sms-gate.app, GitHub capcom6/android-sms-gateway).
In the app turn on “Cloud server” and start the service – a username and password appear.
Enter them above and send a test SMS.
